title: Mixtures and Separation
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Mixtures and Separation Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Classify matter as pure substances or mixtures and investigate techniques for separating mixtures, relating them to the properties of the substances (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on pure substances, mixtures and solutions, and separation techniques: filtration, evaporation, distillation, chromatography and magnetism, with Australian industry examples. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Separate a mixture by a property that differs.
key_sub: Pure substances have one kind of particle; mixtures can be separated by physical methods.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mixtures can be separated because their parts have different properties.

  • Particle size or solubility: filtration (sand from water). Boiling point: evaporation and distillation (salt and water).
  • How far dyes travel on paper: chromatography. Magnetism: iron from sand. Density: panning for gold.
  • A pure substance has only one kind of particle; tap water, air and sea water are mixtures.
Example

Get salt back from salt water?

water evaporates

salt stays behind

Answer: evaporation

Example

Remove iron filings from sand?

iron is magnetic

Answer: a magnet

Common mistakes

  • Thinking filtration removes dissolved salt.
  • Thinking a dissolved solute has disappeared.
  • Calling tap water or air a pure substance.

faq.q: What is the difference between evaporation and distillation?
faq.a: Evaporation removes the solvent to keep the solid, such as salt. Distillation boils the liquid and condenses the vapour to collect the pure liquid.
The solvent moves up the paper and carries each dye a different distance, depending on how soluble it is and how strongly it sticks to the paper.

faq.q: How does Perth get drinking water from the sea?
faq.a: Desalination plants push sea water through very fine membranes (reverse osmosis) that let water through but hold back the salt.

items.q: Can filtration remove dissolved salt from sea water?
c: Only if the water is hot.
No. Dissolved salt particles pass through the filter paper.
items.e: Use evaporation or distillation instead.

items.q: What does distillation use to separate liquids?
items.e: Boil, then condense.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate iron filings from sulfur powder?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which separation technique works on this principle? The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
items.e: This is how evaporation works.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the distillate is correct?
c: It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It measures the temperature of the vapour.
It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
items.e: The distillate is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.

items.q: What is the part of distillation apparatus that cools the gas back into a liquid?
items.e: Cold water flows around it.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the condenser is correct?
c: It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.
It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
items.e: The condenser cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.

items.q: Which method separates an insoluble solid from a liquid?
items.e: Sand from water.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the cold water in the condenser is correct?
c: It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.
It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
They make the liquid boil smoothly.
items.e: The cold water in the condenser flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.

items.q: Why can filtration not remove dissolved salt from sea water?
c: Dissolved salt particles are small enough to pass through filter paper.
Filter paper dissolves in sea water.
items.e: Distillation or reverse osmosis is needed.

items.q: Which separation technique works on this principle? The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapour is cooled and condensed.
items.e: This is how distillation works.

items.q: What happens to salt when it dissolves in water?
c: It breaks into tiny particles that spread between the water particles.
items.e: It is still there.

items.q: Which separation technique works on this principle? Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
items.e: This is how filtration works.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about boiling chips is correct?
c: It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.

It flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.
items.e: Boiling chips make the liquid boil smoothly.

items.q: In reverse osmosis, what is pushed through a partially permeable membrane?
c: water molecules, leaving dissolved salts and impurities behind
items.e: High pressure forces water through.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the residue is correct?
c: It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
It measures the temperature of the vapour.
It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
items.e: The residue is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.

items.q: How can chromatography help to keep food safe?
c: It can show whether a food contains a banned colouring.
items.e: The spots are compared with known dyes.

items.q: What is the filtrate?
c: the liquid that passes through the filter paper
the solid left on the filter paper
items.e: The solid left behind is the residue.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the thermometer is correct?
c: It flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.
It measures the temperature of the vapour.
It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
items.e: The thermometer measures the temperature of the vapour.

items.q: What is the principle behind magnetic attraction?
c: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapour is cooled and condensed.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
items.e: This is how magnetic attraction works.

items.q: What is the principle behind paper chromatography?
c: Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
items.e: This is how paper chromatography works.

items.q: Which separation technique works on this principle? Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
items.e: This is how paper chromatography works.

items.q: What is a mixture?
c: two or more substances that are not chemically joined
items.e: They can be separated.

items.q: Is sea water a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q: Which method is best for separating the dyes in a black marker ink?

items.q: Why is the start line in chromatography drawn in pencil, not pen?
c: Pencil does not dissolve and move up the paper.
items.e: Pen ink would separate too.

items.q: Why must the solvent level be below the start line in paper chromatography?
c: So that the paper does not get wet.
So that the dyes do not dissolve straight into the solvent in the beaker.
So that the dyes move faster.
items.e: The solvent must carry the dyes up the paper.

items.q: Which method is best for separating steel cans and aluminium cans at a recycling plant?
items.e: Steel is attracted to a magnet; aluminium is not.

items.q: Why should a distillation flask never be heated until dry?
c: It could crack or overheat and is unsafe.
items.e: Safety matters in every method.

items.q: How can you get pure dry salt from a mixture of salt and sand?
c: Add water and stir, filter, then evaporate the filtrate.
items.e: Salt dissolves; sand does not.

items.q: Why is distilled water used in car batteries and steam irons?
c: It is pure, with no dissolved solids to leave deposits.
items.e: Uses of pure substances.

items.q: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. A mixture of the two is heated. Which liquid is collected first?
items.e: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils off first.

items.q: Police test the ink on a forged note. Which separation method is mainly used?
c: magnetic separation and separating by density
items.e: Choose the method that matches the property that differs.

items.q: Jack dissolves 15 g of salt in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved when dissolving.

items.q: A recycling plant uses a large magnet on a moving belt. What does it remove?
items.e: Steel contains iron, which is magnetic.

items.q: A student heats copper(II) sulfate solution until it is dry. Why might she stop before it is completely dry?
c: To get crystals instead of a powder that may decompose with too much heat.
To make it a liquid again.
items.e: Heat gently and let crystals form as it cools.

items.q: Mia has a mixture of salt, sand and iron filings. Which order of steps separates all three?
c: magnet, then dissolve in water and filter, then evaporate
items.e: Remove iron first, then use solubility.

items.q: How would you get pure, dry salt from rock salt (salt mixed with sand and grit)?
c: Dissolve in water, filter, then evaporate the filtrate.
items.e: Three steps.

items.q: In a chromatogram, a food colouring gives two spots. What does this show?
c: It is a mixture of two dyes.
items.e: A pure dye gives only one spot.
